approval_provenance.decision_rationale: I approve the narrowly bounded compatibility exception for the two original ACS 2024 source packages associated with the August 2026 monthly cycle. My decision is to preserve the original August source identities and data lineage while completing the historical-data recovery and corrected Macro reconstruction. I understand that the original acquisition was performed under a different monthly refresh policy and that some original evidence cannot be independently recovered, including normalized snapshot bytes, complete HTTP response evidence, and the original manifest Git SHA. I accept those documented assurance limitations for these exact two packages only, based on the technical qualification and verification results presented for review. I understand that monthly no-content classifications are process-attested rather than independently confirmed Census omissions. ACS5 fallback is restricted to the 67 recorded ACS5-only geographies, and the four jointly unobserved geographies must remain missing without imputation. I consider this exception proportionate because these are historical August artifacts, and future monthly refreshes will provide opportunities to acquire and validate newer data under the current process. Those refreshes do not retroactively establish the missing August evidence. I authorize preparation of a separately reviewed compatibility-registry installation change following successful live verification of this decision. This approval does not authorize merging that installation change, historical physical-state acceptance, Source Set publication, serving promotion, Macro execution, broader-vintage exceptions, or future acquisition under the original policy.

The retained official Census documentation states that standard 2020 ACS 1-year estimates were not released because pandemic-related collection disruption and nonresponse bias prevented the standard estimates from meeting statistical quality standards. I approve treating standard ACS1 2020 as a whole-vintage nonpublication gap, supported by the exact documentary capture and subject commitments below. The experimental 2020 ACS1 estimates are a different product and must not substitute for the standard release; the separately published ACS5 product is unaffected. This classification is not inferred from a missing acquisition, an HTTP response, or individual-geography absence. It does not authorize fabricated observations, imputation, physical-state acceptance, or activation.

limitations: No API endpoint response or dataset discovery result is asserted.
Documentation supports standard-product nonpublication, not provider-ineligibility of individual geographies.
Human evidence review and separate scope approval remain required.

approval_provenance.decision_rationale: I approve the initial ACS5 historical governance scope of 2009 through 2024 inclusive, with all 16 vintages expected available and no governed whole-vintage gaps. The missing 2023 acquisition remains an acquisition-recovery obligation and must not be reclassified as provider nonpublication or removed from the expected inventory. Standard ACS1 2020 nonpublication does not create an ACS5 gap. This decision preserves ACS5 product identity and the exact existing metrics, 223 requested geographies, ten exclusions, configuration digests, and limitations below. It establishes intended governed scope, not verified package availability, complete observations, or accepted physical history. Compatibility authorization, acquisition recovery, materialization, publication, serving, and Macro remain subject to their separate authority and operational gates.

I approve the initial ACS1 historical governance scope of 2005 through 2024 inclusive. The 19 expected-available vintages and separately governed standard ACS1 2020 nonpublication gap form the complete, nonoverlapping vintage partition committed by this subject. The approval is limited to the existing population and median-household-income metrics, 223 requested geographies, ten explicit exclusions, configuration digests, and limitations below. The final installed scope must reference the separately approved gap after its identity is recomputed with genuine provenance. Scope approval does not assert acquisition completeness, original-package verification, provider eligibility for individual geographies, or physical-state acceptance. It does not approve the separate 2024 compatibility exception or alter accepted August identities.
